stem: Why must steroids be strictly avoided if a child has active Herpes Simplex keratitis involving the corneal epithelium?

options.text: Steroids can cause viral particles to enter the corneal stroma, leading to scarring and vision loss.
Steroids stimulate the rapid replication of the virus on the eyelid skin.
Steroids interfere with the absorption of oral acyclovir medication.
Steroids permanently stain the cornea when combined with the HSV virus.

explanation: Steroid use can drive the infection deeper into the stroma, triggering an antigen-antibody reaction that results in permanent scarring.
rationale: Think about how the medication might change the location of the infection within the layers of the eye.

optionExplanations.A: Steroid use can drive the infection deeper into the stroma, triggering an antigen-antibody reaction that results in permanent scarring.
optionExplanations.B: The concern with steroids is the deep penetration into the corneal tissue, rather than the replication on the skin of the lids.
optionExplanations.C: There is no known pharmacological interference between topical steroids and the absorption of oral antivirals.
optionExplanations.D: The issue is biological scarring from an inflammatory reaction, not a staining process.
